moat_against: People business at the profit core: producers own client relationships and can walk to rivals; no owned asset or network effect locks in the fee pool
Cyclicality is un-moated: conservative OE collapsed in the 2023 rate-shock transaction freeze
Sophisticated institutional clients negotiate fees hard; pricing power unproven through a full cycle
Growth increasingly bought via M&A (Pearce ~$1.2B, Industrious) — goodwill/integration risk, flatters reported growth
AI/automation threatens standardized valuation, brokerage and reporting tasks with no proven durable tech edge
moat_for: Global #1 at scale across leasing, sales, outsourcing and investment management simultaneously — no rival matches the breadth
Recurring facilities-management/outsourcing contracts embedded in client operations, plus project-management and IM fees — real switching costs
Largest managed portfolio and transaction dataset in the industry; scale funds tech/AI spend smaller rivals cannot match
Diversification across property types and geographies softened the 2023 trough vs a pure brokerage
moat_justification: Global #1 CRE services scale and breadth, recurring facilities/outsourcing + project management + investment management mix with real switching costs, unmatched data/talent density — against a people-based advisory core whose producers can walk, un-moated transaction cyclicality (conservative OE total fell to $79M in 2023), hard-negotiating institutional clients, and growth increasingly bought via M&A (Pearce, Industrious).
name: CBRE Group, Inc.
one_liner: No. 1 global CRE services franchise, moat 6/10 — but at $129.67 (OE yield 2.75% on normalized OE of $3.57/sh) the weighted IRR is just 6.42% with IV@15% of $37.94; even the super-bull case only reaches 10.07%, so it clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$37.94.
